entry.title: Taxpayers Not Penalised for Inaccurate Intermediary-Submitted Income Data
entry.summary: Taxpayers won’t be penalised because of inaccurate details submitted by intermediaries IRAS · Oct 5, 2026 · GuidanceIRAS states that taxpayers will not be penalised if tax assessments must be revised due to incomplete or inaccurate income information submitted by intermediaries, who are responsible for accuracy. Following Grab's correction of income records, IRAS is revising assessments for affected private-hire car drivers and will issue revised tax bills, requiring no action from drivers before receipt.

entry.title: Simpler tax, stronger business: new digital tools to ease 2026 corporate income tax filing
entry.summary: Tax Made Simple; Business Made Stronger: New Digital Resources to Ease Corporate Income Tax Filing in 2026 IRAS · Oct 19, 2026 · GuidanceThe Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has introduced new and enhanced digital self-help tools to make it easier for companies to file their Corporate Income Tax returns for Year of Assessment 2026. The filing deadline is 30 November. IRAS also reminds companies that late filers may be fined and that directors are responsible for accurate and timely filing.

entry.title: IRAS warns against false or unsupported employment expense claims
entry.summary: IRAS Warns Against False, Incorrect or Unsupported Employment Expense Claims IRAS · Oct 21, 2026 · GuidanceThe Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has found misleading information circulating that encourages taxpayers to claim employment expenses not incurred or not tax deductible. Taxpayers are told to ensure their claims are valid, accurate and supported by records. IRAS has identified over 3,000 taxpayers making similar claims, unsupported claims will be disallowed, and deliberate false claims may face penalties and enforcement action.
